title: Mad Libs Generator
story: 'The ADJECTIVE NOUN VERBed over the ADJECTIVE NOUN.' Fill in the blanks: 'The purple elephant danced over the giant pizza.' Mad Libs turn grammar into comedy. Build a generator that takes words and stitches them into hilarious stories.
why: Mad Libs generator teaches string templating and replacement — replacing placeholders with user-provided words in a structured narrative.
analogy: A coloring book where you pick the colors but the outline is fixed. The story template is the outline — the structure never changes. Your word choices are the crayons — they make each story unique. Same skeleton, infinite skins.
expected_output:
The sparkly unicorn dances gracefully every day.
The grumpy dragon sleeps loudly every day.
The tiny robot computes tirelessly every day.
try_it: Create 5 different story templates. Add a random template selector that picks one at random. Support more word types: PLURAL_NOUN, COLOR, NUMBER, BODY_PART. Build a word bank for each type so the program can auto-generate funny stories.
tips: Use descriptive placeholders like ADJ, NOUN, VERB — easy to find and replace
Build story strings piece by piece with string.str_concat
Keep templates separate from filling logic — swap templates without changing code
common_mistakes: Forgetting spaces between words — each concatenation needs proper spacing
Not handling plural vs singular verb forms (dance vs dances)
Hardcoding a single template — the fun is in variety
